source.title: SafeSteer: A Decoding-level Defense Mechanism for Multimodal Large Language Models
source.authors: Xinyi Zeng; Xue Yang; Jingyuan Zhang; Huanqian Yan; Xiang Chen; Kaiwen Wei; Hankun Kang; Yu Tian

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses MLLMs’ purported decoding-stage safety discrimination to build a decoding-level defense, but does not test the claim’s fine-tuning, KL-concentration, bypass, parameter-localization, or safety-deepening versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative hidden-state visualizations of harmful/harmless inputs and outputs; these are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version because they are not per-token KL measurements or harmful-completion rates. The SafeSteer ASR tables, ablations, and hyperparameter results concern the performance of the study’s own defense, not tests of the claim’s interventions. The probe’s training loss is not a result about the claim.
record.test_reason: The study builds a decoding-level defense (SafeSteer) that relies on refusals appearing in early tokens. Its results are its own method's ASR, and qualitative hidden-state plots. It reports no per-token KL between aligned and base models, no fine-tuning attacks, no prefill bypass, no parameter localization and no deepening training. The early-step separability plots concern representation separability, not KL or compliance rates, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that MLLMs can distinguish harmful from harmless inputs during decoding and that image-based attacks are more stealthy. SafeSteer, a probe-based token reranker plus a modal alignment vector, improves safety (up to 33.4%) without fine-tuning or loss of effectiveness.
record.recipe_differences: This is a multimodal decoding-level defense that trains a lightweight probe and adds a modality-alignment vector; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or per-token KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that image-based inputs are more stealthy than text-based inputs and that latent-space separation becomes less distinct at later decoding steps. Its defense hyperparameter analysis varies top-k and the number of decoding steps, but those results concern SafeSteer performance rather than the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Prefill-stage hidden states separate harmful from harmless inputs in Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL (qualitative).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLLM prefill representations linearly separate harmful and harmless inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful, refusal and harmless output tokens are separable in early decoding steps; the boundary blurs at later steps (qualitative).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MLLMs, harmfulness discriminability of output representations is concentrated in early decoding steps.

fits_no_version.finding: Image-based (SD) harmful inputs sit closer to the harmless cluster than text-based (CB) harmful inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image-modality harmful inputs carry weaker harmfulness representations than text equivalents in MLLM decoders.

fits_no_version.finding: Applying the probe at more decoding steps does not significantly improve safety. Authors attribute this to refusals being set in the initial tokens (Appendix A, Fig. 6; no numbers in text).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intervening on the first few decoding steps captures most of the obtainable safety gain for decoding-time defenses.

record.problems: The representation findings are qualitative visualizations without numeric separation measures or reported uncertainty. They do not directly measure harmful-request compliance or per-token KL divergence.
record.rows_left_out: SafeSteer main results and ablations in Tables 1 and 3, plus its hyperparameter results in Appendix A, were left out because they report the study’s own defense performance rather than outcomes testing the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models. Only qualitative early-step representation separability is shown.
No prefill or suffix bypass tested. Image-based attacks are evaluated only as inputs to the defense.
No training-based deepening. SafeSteer is an inference-time reranking applied at early steps.

record.verdict_notes: The record's rows and their links are acceptable; all rows correctly link to none. The Appendix A step-hyperparameter observation is defense-performance evidence and was reasonably left out. It is noted under fits_no_version only as context for the early-token idea.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or harmful-request compliance rates.
No fine-tuning on benign instruction data or resulting harmful compliance rates.
No per-token KL divergence comparison between aligned and base models.
No test of compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses of refusal. The paper uses decoding changes as a defense.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
No test of whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
No training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens, or evaluation of whether such training holds up.
